explanation: L4/H4 is a word-start copy head: at nearly every position its attention is one-hot (weight about 1) on a single earlier token, and that token is the first subword piece of a word - the leading-space piece that opens a word, or the capitalised segment of a camelCase identifier. Its write is a copy of that piece, so strength is set mainly by which piece it copies rather than by the token at the peak (attended-piece identity explains 92% of the strength variance over the scan's top examples, the peak token 52%): copying the first piece of a multi-piece word (a name, place, foreign or technical term, or any longer word's stem, e.g. ' Kl', ' Kad', ' Wyn', ' Od', ' China') writes 1.0-2.5 of the 2.51 maximum and crosses the 0.63 line on 83-93% of such positions, while copying a single-token whole word or a mid-word continuation stays near the head's mean (mean 0.16-0.35, 12-28% above the line); multi-piece words are everywhere, so about 40% of scanned tokens are active in every scanned language and in code, and the correct reading is broad - predict ordinary longer or structured prose active-weak to active (0.4-2.0), and predict inactive (0.0-0.3) for short one- or two-clause sentences of common single-piece words (up to about 12 tokens, e.g. 'The cat sat on the mat.'; 39 of 40 such sentences measured below 0.3).
